questions.q: What does Flow Orchestration add on top of the other flow types covered in this course?
options: Faster SOQL query performance for all flows
A replacement for the Decision element inside a single flow
The ability to coordinate a multi-stage, often multi-person business process by sequencing multiple flows
Automatic bulkification of any flow it touches
questions.explain: Flow Orchestration coordinates a process too long or too people-dependent for one flow interview, by sequencing other flows into stages and steps.

questions.q: What is a 'stage' in Flow Orchestration?
options: A single element on the canvas representing one database operation
A type of fault path specific to orchestrations
A synonym for a flow version
A named grouping of related steps; only one stage can be in progress per record at a time
questions.explain: A stage groups related steps together, and an orchestration can have multiple stages, but only one is actively in progress for a given record at once.

questions.q: What's the difference between an interactive step and a background step?
options: An interactive step runs a screen flow and requires a person to act; a background step runs an autolaunched flow with no human interaction
There is no functional difference, only a label
Interactive steps run faster than background steps
Background steps can only be used in record-triggered flows
questions.explain: Interactive steps show up as work items someone must open and complete (screen flow); background steps execute automatically (autolaunched flow).

questions.q: On an orchestration's canvas, what does the Add Element menu offer?
options: Every standard Flow element, like Decision, Loop, and Assignment
Only Background Step and Interactive Step
Stage and Decision
Only Stage
questions.explain: Orchestration logic is built at a different altitude than ordinary flow elements — the canvas offers Stage and Decision as the building blocks.

questions.q: As of February 2026, what changed about Flow Orchestration's availability?
options: It was discontinued in favor of Apex-only solutions
It became available only to Enterprise Edition orgs
It merged permanently into Process Builder
It became a standard Flow type included for all customers at no additional cost, instead of requiring a separate paid add-on
questions.explain: Salesforce made Flow Orchestration a standard Flow type in February 2026, removing the paid add-on requirement that previously limited its use.
